problem.title: Two Sum
problem.description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.
constraints: You may not use the same element twice.

example3_duplicates.danger: Reusing the same element at index 0 (3 + 3 = 6 with single element), or overwriting duplicate keys in naive 2-pass hash map.

bruteForce.mechanism: Nested loops checking every pair (i, j) where j > i.
bruteForce.drawback: Quadratic growth becomes unacceptable for large arrays (e.g. 10,000 elements requires ~50,000,000 operations).

onePassHashMap.mechanism: For each element nums[i], calculate complement = target - nums[i]. Check if complement exists in Hash Map. If found, return [map[complement], i]. Otherwise, store map[nums[i]] = i.
onePassHashMap.criticalDetail: Check complement BEFORE inserting the current number to avoid self-pairing on duplicates like [3, 3] with target 6.

educationalGoals: Visualize array indices vs values clearly in 3D.
Contrast O(n^2) nested scanning pointers with O(1) hash map instant lookup.
Explain mathematical complement formula: complement = target - nums[i].
Highlight common traps: value vs index, self-pairing, duplicate keys.
Demonstrate classic time-space tradeoff: O(n) space trading for O(n) time.
